contextual.summary: Exeter makes lower contextual offers (usually two grades below the typical offer, three for care-experienced applicants) to applicants who meet any one of its published criteria.
contextual.typicalReduction: Two-grade adjustment for most criteria; three-grade adjustment for care leavers and care-experienced applicants; up to three grades for progression-programme participants and refugees/asylum seekers

criteria.detail: Live in a low-participation area (POLAR4 quintile 1 or 2) and attend a state school — two grades
Live in a low-participation area (TUNDRA MSOA quintile 1 or 2) and attend a state school — two grades
Live in an area of deprivation (IMD quintile 1 or 2) and attend a state school — two grades

Attend a non-selective state school or college in the South West or Wales on Exeter's Contextual Offer Schools and Colleges List (PDF: https://www.exeter.ac.uk/v8media/recruitmentsites/documents/20278_UoE_Contextual_Offer_Schools_Colleges_List.pdf) — two grades
Have received free school meals and attend a state school — two grades
Applying from an Elephant Group school, completed the Bridges to HE programme, or did activity with an IntoUniversity centre in Years 10–13 — two grades
SEREN partnership (Wales) participants who completed a Seren Academic Challenge Series or the SEREN University of Exeter Residential — two grades
Care leaver or care experienced — three grades

Registered on a progression programme run or managed by Exeter: Exeter Scholars, Realising Opportunities, Sutton Trust Pathways to Law (in person and online), Sutton Trust Pathways to Banking & Finance (online), Mature Access Pathway — up to three grades
Seeking asylum, limited leave to remain and from a state school, humanitarian protection, or refugee status — up to three grades

contextual.rulesText: You are eligible for a contextual offer if you meet one of the criteria; the application process is still competitive so an offer isn't guaranteed. Where courses have specific subject requirements, grade adjustments may differ, and GCSE requirements are not reduced.

source.evidence: You are eligible for a contextual offer at a lower grade than our typical entry requirements if you meet one of the criteria below

programmes.name: Exeter Scholars – Year 12 South West On-Campus Pathway (Business strand)
programmes.summary: Exeter's access programme for Year 12 students living in the South West: six on-campus subject sessions in 2027 (including a Business: Finance, Economics, Management and Entrepreneurship strand) plus a student conference.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 state school students living in Devon, Cornwall, Somerset, Bristol or Dorset who meet the GCSE and fee-status requirements and at least one widening participation criterion.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: State school (or home-educated, or fee-paying on a full bursary), Year 12, at least 8 GCSEs at 9–4 including Maths and English at 4+, Home/EU fee status, plus at least one of: low HE progression neighbourhood; low-income neighbourhood; low participation of state-school pupils (by postcode); free school meals; eligible for school bursaries; parents didn't go to university; care experienced; young carer; disability; estranged; refugee or asylum seeker. Business strand: GCSE Maths grade 5 (or A/AS-level Maths) and GCSE English Language grade 4.
benefits: Guaranteed offer from Exeter (subject to subject-specific and GCSE requirements) with up to a three-grade reduction (3 A-level grades below the standard offer for most courses for 2026 entry)
Travel costs for programme activities refunded
Senior Scholar benefits package if you pass the online assessment and study at Exeter
programmes.offerReduction: Up to three A-level grades below the typical offer (2027 contextual policy); guaranteed offer subject to subject and GCSE requirements
programmes.subjects: Business: Finance, Economics, Management and Entrepreneurship (other strands available)

runs.text: Six sessions between January and October/November 2027 (4 at Streatham, Exeter; 2 at Penryn, Cornwall; dates TBC) plus the Exeter Scholars Student Conference

programmes.infoNote: On-Campus Pathway 2026–2028 cohort (applications autumn 2026, sessions during 2027). Session dates for the Business strand are TBC.

notes: All courses listed are taught at the Streatham Campus, Exeter (University of Exeter Business School).

BSc Economics and BSc Economics and Finance need A-level Maths at grade B; Business Economics, Economics and Politics, PPE, Accounting and Finance and Business and Management have no A-level subject requirement (GCSE Maths 5–7 instead).
Exeter gives up to a three-grade contextual adjustment to participants of Realising Opportunities, Sutton Trust Pathways to Law and Sutton Trust Pathways to Banking & Finance (online).
Exeter Scholars has three Year 12 routes: South West on-campus (Devon, Cornwall, Somerset, Bristol, Dorset), Virtual (UK-wide) and National residential (outside the South West).
